text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Turnover in the retail sector grows 5.4 percent in July, year-on-year, according to central bureau of statistics. (page 5).
- Zaandam based food retailier Ahold says net profit jumps 18 percent to 121.3 million guilders on 15.8 percent higher turnover. (page 1)
- Cabinet retreats on wealth tax plans, agrees to amend proposals to raise taxes on owner/directors of private firms. (page 1).
- The government's plan to prune pensions is not well-thought out and will have unintended effects, say two corporate pensions funds associations. (page 1).
- Construction firm NBM Amstelland reports net profit more than doubled in the first half to 33.6 million guilders. (page 4).
VOLKSKRANT
- Jules Wijdenbosch, a candidate from the National Democratic Party of Desi Bouterse, wins Suriname's presidential election.
(page 1).
- Philips Electronics sells its producer of electronmicroscopes to FEI Company of the U.S. in exchange for 55 percent of the shares in FEI. (page 2).
- Casema, the Netherlands' biggest cable TV company begins pay television on October 1. (page 3).
- Electrical equipment maker Holec to concentrate all its activities in Hengelo, plans to build a 100 million guilder factory at the Twentekanaal business complex. (page 15).
DE TELEGRAAF
- Big interest in new Dutch telephone licences. Communications ministry has three serious applications and a fourth is on its way. (page 25).
- Amsterdam bourse to set up market for young, fast growing businesses. (page 25).
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD

- Economy minister Hans Wijers says all trends in the Dutch economy moving in the right direction, in response to "The Dutch Economy in 1995," -- a report from the central bureau for statistics. (page 13).
- Dutch businesses spend relatively more on art sponsorship than businesses in Germany, Great Britain, France and the United States, a study shows (page 1).
- Independent supermarts last year booked a profits growth of more than 15 percent (page 14).
